exact_proposed_claim: Pre-execution monitoring detects hijacked tool calls before harmful execution under split-conformal thresholding.
relevant_literature_contrast: Differs from DriftNet and TraceAegis which perform offline post-execution auditing after side-effects execute
limitations_and_caveats: Hijacked test sample is compact (N=3); confidence interval is wide; bounded to AgentDojo workspace tasks
defensible_wording: Under the tested AgentDojo workspace benchmark, AgentWatch-A detected all 3 held-out hijacked trajectories before the first harmful tool executed.

exact_proposed_claim: Goal conditioning and argument provenance prevent the catastrophic false interruptions suffered by simpler sequence and content monitors.
supporting_evidence: Track 2 Live Runs: run-b1-live-01 to run-gru-full-01
uncertainty_and_ci: Absolute Risk Reduction ARR = 1.00 (vs B1/B4) and 0.50 (vs B3); Fisher p=0.167
relevant_literature_contrast: Directly challenges LlamaFirewall observation-only scanning and Trajectory Guard unconditioned sequence modeling
limitations_and_caveats: Track 2 live scenario count is N=2 per condition; Fisher exact test cannot reach p<0.05 on N=2 despite 0 vs 2 difference
defensible_wording: In closed-loop evaluation, goal-conditioned recurrence and provenance eliminated the 100% false interruption rate suffered by unconditioned sequence and bigram baselines.

exact_proposed_claim: Split-conformal calibration on benign trajectory maxima controls the empirical false alarm rate on held-out tasks.
relevant_literature_contrast: Extends Vovk et al. and Angelopoulos & Bates split-conformal quantile calibration to multi-step agent trajectory maxima
limitations_and_caveats: Calibration sample size n=5 produces order statistic k=5 (the maximum); empirical test FPR of 40% exceeds target alpha=0.20 due to small-sample variance
defensible_wording: Calibrating on benign trajectory maxima provides an empirical distribution-free thresholding mechanism, though finite calibration sample size (n=5) yields wide empirical coverage variation.

exact_proposed_claim: AgentWatch-A achieves sub-2ms per-decision CPU inference latency without requiring cloud LLM tokens.
supporting_evidence: In-loop timer profiling on Intel/AMD x86_64 CPU
point_estimate: Mean CPU latency = 1.61 ms; p95 = 1.91 ms; Max = 1.94 ms
uncertainty_and_ci: Deterministic standard deviation = 0.18 ms across 20 evaluated steps
relevant_literature_contrast: Contrasts with AgentSentry and LLM-as-a-judge runtime guards which incur 200-800ms API latency and dollar costs
limitations_and_caveats: Latency evaluated on local consumer CPU; heavily loaded systems or massive vocabularies may exhibit slight latency increase
defensible_wording: AgentWatch-A executes at an average CPU latency of 1.61 ms per proposed tool call with zero cloud token overhead.
